newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish moderately higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish moderately higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures recovered from a quick morning selloff to finish moderately higher but off session peaks.
Afternoon trading remained relatively light, with prices gradually heading higher after the morning's rally from sizable opening losses.
"The market's rally during the course of the day...was a sneaky move up, subtle," said a floor broker in Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures.
The US T-bond futures recovery from the days lows gave shorts impetus to cover and guided prices higher,traders said.

T-bond futures jumped after the Federal Reserve's Beige Book said the U.S. economy seems to be expanding moderately with no clear sign of higher inflation, although there appears to be greater upward pressure on wages than on prices.
Traders noted with some relief that the report did not indicate more upward pressure on prices.
They also said equities' resilience continued to impress those who had expected a pullback from recent strength.
"I think in general the market had gotten oversold," said a stock index futures floor analyst. "We had a lot of selling into the (jobs) number...but just can't sustain a break."

"I think there's a short interest in this market and bonds are discounting a quarter-point hike," he said, noting that traders appear to expect a 25-basis-point rise in rates from the September 24 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Futures had fallen at the outset, weighed down by news that Iraqi forces fired one or two missiles at U.S. fighter jets over northern Iraq on Wednesday.

Additional pressure stemmed from an initial pullback in Motorola stock, which fell after it forecast a disappointing third quarter that it said could fall below second-quarter levels and analysts' estimates.
Motorola stock subsequently recouped the bulk of those losses, allowing stocks to float upward as oil-related issues benefitted from firmness in crude oil on the Iraqi tensions.

T-bond futures also dropped early on rate-hike nerves that were heightened by a Washington Post interview with Federal Reserve governor Janet Yellen that reiterated some points made in a Reuters interview with her published on Tuesday.
She said in the Post interview that she was "nervous about the diminishing slack in labor markets" but noted there has been "virtually no evidence of inflation pressures outside of food and energy."
Traders also waited for Thursday's August U.S. producer price index, expected to firm 0.1 percent overall and in the core rate.
December S&P 500 futures become the new lead contract at the beginning of Thursday's pit-trading session, traders said.

September S&P 500s rose 1.90 pts to 667.00, Value Lines firmed 0.70 to 623.20, Midcap 400s added 1.40 pts to 234.05, NYSE Composite firmed 0.90 to 357.85, and Nikkei 225 fell 105.0 to 20,520.0. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
